name: Polar
summary: A developer-focused Merchant of Record for software, digital products, subscriptions, usage billing, and built-in benefits.

pricing.headline: Current Starter pricing is 5% + $0.50; eligible Early Member organizations retain grandfathered pricing.
pricing.assumptions: Current Starter plan for organizations created on or after May 27, 2026 (5% + $0.50). Optional paid plans on Polar's pricing page: Pro $20/mo at 3.8% + 40¢, Growth $100/mo at 3.6% + 35¢, and Scale $400/mo at 3.4% + 30¢. Payout and cross-border conversion costs are separate from transaction FX; legacy Early Member rates are grandfathered.

currencySupport.presentment: Products can carry explicit prices in 130+ currencies; checkout selects an enabled local price by customer location.
currencySupport.customerCharge: The buyer pays in the selected presentment currency. If it is not enabled on the product, checkout falls back to the organization's default.
currencySupport.settlement: Every order is converted into a USD Polar balance; Stripe Connect can then pay that balance to the seller's connected account currency.
currencySupport.buyerFx: No separately published local-currency conversion markup; a 1.5% non-US-card fee is passed through to the seller instead.
currencySupport.merchantFx: This can be a two-conversion route: the order converts to USD, then a non-USD payout converts again. Only the payout conversion fee is explicit: 0.25% in the EU or up to 1% elsewhere, plus Stripe payout fees.
currencySupport.moneyPath: buyer currency → USD balance → payout currency

marketExamples.path: USD charge → USD balance → USD payout
marketExamples.cost: The currencies remain USD. Standard transaction and Stripe payout fees still apply.

marketExamples.path: EUR charge → USD balance → EUR payout
marketExamples.cost: No separate first-conversion fee is published; EU payout FX is 0.25%, and the seller also absorbs Polar's non-US-card fee.

marketExamples.path: CHF charge → USD balance → CHF payout
marketExamples.cost: No separate first-conversion fee is published; payout FX outside the EU is up to 1%, plus the non-US-card and Stripe payout fees.

sellerCoverage: Polar supports individual and business payouts in its published country list through Stripe Connect Express.
buyerCoverage: Payments are accepted globally except from documented sanctioned countries, subject to payment-method availability.
products: Eligible software, SaaS, digital products, subscriptions, usage-based products, and developer-oriented benefits.

features.checkout: Hosted and embedded checkout with API-created sessions.
features.subscriptions: Recurring, usage-based, seat-based, trial, and multi-currency pricing features.
features.invoicing: Automatic order invoices and EU B2B reverse-charge handling; advanced quoting should be verified for the use case.
features.paymentMethods: Cards, wallets, and local methods documented by Polar and its payment partners.
features.payouts: Stripe Connect Express payouts with documented payout and cross-border costs.

responsibilities.area: Indirect-tax calculation, registration, filing, and remittance
responsibilities.note: Polar describes itself as reseller and tax-liable seller for covered transactions.
Polar manages network exposure and charges a documented dispute fee.
The seller owns the product relationship; Polar can automate benefit grants.
Net payouts still require business accounting and income-tax reporting.

strengths: Built-in usage, seat, and entitlement features
limitations: Younger operating history than long-established providers
Brazil is not on the current supported seller-country list
Additional international, payout, and dispute costs matter
bestFor: SaaS needing usage or benefit-based billing
avoidIf: You require a long enterprise operating history
Your seller country or product is outside Polar policy
